d: The Facilities & HSE Officer – Automotive oversees daily maintenance, physical security, and environmental health and safety compliance across automotive facilities (dealership showrooms, service workshops, body shops, and spare parts warehouses). This role manages facility uptime, HVAC and shop equipment operations, hazardous material storage, workshop environmental compliance, and safety auditing. The primary objective is to maintain a high-standard, operational, safe, and fully compliant workplace for technicians, showroom staff, and customers.
q: Bachelor’s degree or Diploma in Engineering (Mechanical or Electrical), Environmental Health & Safety (EHS), or related technical fields.
NEBOSH IGC or OSHA 30-hour certification required. Valid First Aid/CPR and Fire Warden certifications.
Familiarity with ISO 14001 (Environmental) and ISO 45001 (Occupational Health & Safety) standards.
5–7 years of hands-on experience in property maintenance, contractor oversight, and health & safety enforcement in corporate, commercial, or automotive multi-site settings.

Sound knowledge of civil, electrical, and mechanical infrastructure; expertise in life-safety systems (CCTV, fire alarms, sprinklers); proficiency in hazardous material/waste management and risk assessments (JSA).
Proven track record in evaluating contractors, negotiating SLAs for cost efficiency, overseeing cleaning/security operations, and coordinating office onboarding logistics.
Strong leadership and communication skills, decisive crisis management during operational disruptions or safety incidents, and meticulous record-keeping abilities.
r: Oversee and resolve all operational, structural, and infrastructure issues across company premises.
Conduct frequent physical inspections of properties to identify operational defects, managing and executing mechanical, electrical, and civil works requested by General Managers.
Analyze, scope, and process approvals for civil, mechanical, and electrical requests across divisions before execution.

Inspect, maintain, and ensure the full operational readiness of all life-safety and security systems, including CCTV, fire alarms, fire hose reels, smoke sensors, heat detectors, and water sprinklers.
Identify technical issues with life-safety equipment and liaise with specialized fire safety contractors (such as Alpha Fire Co. or Gulf Services Co.) for prompt rectification.
Develop, test, and maintain operational contingency plans to mitigate business disruptions and safeguard daily continuity.
Coordinate with Group HSE & Admin personnel to oversee concurrent multi-site projects and vendor activities without interrupting core business operations.
Coordinate with all external suppliers, contractors, and service providers to ensure deliverables meet contractual standards and organizational requirements.
Negotiate service terms with contractors, maintenance firms, and suppliers to secure competitive pricing, high quality, and economies of scale.
Conduct timely supplier evaluations for all maintenance service providers across divisions to ensure performance compliance.
Supervise fire protection contractors, verifying that all works comply with approved technical specifications and that Annual Maintenance Contracts (AMCs) are renewed on schedule.
Manage the commercial approval process and legal formalities for the disposal and sale of scrap materials.
Supervise security personnel across all corporate sites to ensure property protection and access control.
Manage direct line supervision over maintenance and janitorial staff across company properties.
Enforce cleaning, hygiene, and aesthetic standards across all premises to maintain corporate brand uniformity.
Provision and arrange all necessary logistical support, office furniture, and workstations for new hires based on HR notifications and department requirements.
Ensure full organizational compliance with all local HSE laws, regulatory standards, and internal safety protocols.
Maintain comprehensive records of all workplace HSE incidents, forwarding detailed accident and near-miss reports to the Division General Manager, Group HR & Admin Manager, and Division HR.
Lead incident investigations as directed by leadership, conducting root-cause analyses and issuing corrective action plans.
Attend monthly executive management meetings, representing administrative operations and resolving department-specific challenges.
Execute special projects, strategic assignments, and operational tasks directed by the Managing Director, General Manager, or Group HR & Admin Manager.

d: The Supply Chain Executive will be responsible for managing the end-to-end supply chain operations for LaSavista within the UAE, ensuring efficient importation, compliance, and distribution of products. Based in the Dubai Free Zone, this role plays a critical part in supporting the transition from imported finished goods to locally produced solutions via co-manufacturing, ensuring continuity, efficiency, and scalability of supply.
r: Own and manage end-to-end supply chain activities from supplier to customer delivery
Coordinate international shipments, ensuring timely and cost-effective delivery
Manage inventory levels to ensure product availability while minimizing working capital
Drive continuous improvement in logistics efficiency and cost control
Ensure full compliance with UAE import regulations and Free Zone requirements
Manage documentation, customs clearance, and regulatory processes
Liaise with Free Zone authorities and third-party logistics providers
Maintain accurate records for audits and internal compliance
Ensure all LaSavista / ADM products comply with UAE sugar tax regulations, including proper classification, documentation, and labeling requirements
Liaise with local tax authorities to manage sugar tax compliance, reporting, and any related regulatory updates
Support onboarding and ongoing management of regional co-manufacturers
Coordinate production planning and material supply with co-manufacturing partners
Monitor performance, quality, and service levels of co-manufacturers
Act as the key link between internal teams and external manufacturing partners
Develop demand and supply plans in collaboration with commercial teams
Monitor stock levels, forecasts, and replenishment cycles
Track and report key supply chain metrics and KPIs
Provide insights and recommendations to improve supply chain performance

Geographic Scope: Primary focus on GCC markets, with particular emphasis on the UAE and KSA as core operating hubs. The role will also support expansion into additional high-growth international markets as LaSavista continues to scale its global footprint
Supply Base: UK and Europe based suppliers transitioning to regional co-manufacturers
Logistics Flow: International imports + local production and distribution
Internal Stakeholders: EU Supply Chain and Co-Man teams, Sales, Marketing, Finance, Leadership teams
External Stakeholders: Freight forwarders, Free Zone authorities, co-manufacturers, suppliers
Regional & Global Supply Chain & Co-Man teams
ERP / CRM systems and data analysis
Ability to operate in a fast-paced, evolving environment
University degree in Business management, Engineering or Supply Chain
Minimum 10 years’ experience as Supply Chain Manager for an international Food / Beverage Company
IT savvy and very comfortable with numbers, know how to analyze complex data and provide meaningful information.
Broad experience within ME region, especially regarding compliance, import and export procedures as well as legal requirements

Teamwork, effective collaboration with peers. A self-starter, able to make an impact and thrive with the independence offered to her/him. Problem solver, resilient and flexible. Entrepreneurial & Focus to “get the job done”. Excellent communication skills.
Fluent in Arabic and Good level in English.
Forecast accuracy and stock planning effectiveness
